title: Lamb shish kabob with vegetables (no potatoes)

content.title: About
content.content: Lamb shish kabob with vegetables (no potatoes) is made from tender lamb cubes marinated in spices and a mix of fresh vegetables (bell pepper, zucchini, onion, cherry tomatoes). The pieces are threaded onto skewers and grilled over high heat until a fragrant crust forms. The dish is rich in protein, vitamins and minerals while omitting starchy potatoes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lamb is a staple in Middle Eastern and Mediterranean cuisines.
Marinades often contain yogurt, which tenderizes the meat and adds probiotics.
Vegetables grilled alongside the meat retain their juices, giving the kabob vivid color and moisture.
Quick high‑heat grilling preserves most of the nutrients in both meat and veg.
The dish is commonly served with tzatziki or a mint‑yogurt sauce.

items.title: High‑quality protein source
items.content: Lamb provides complete animal protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals support immune function and hemoglobin formation.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Lamb contains B12, niacin and riboflavin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from vegetables
items.content: Bell peppers and tomatoes are high in vitamin C and carotenoids that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Excluding potatoes makes the dish suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic or intolerant to lamb.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Lamb contains saturated fats; people with heart disease should monitor portion size.

items.title: Risk of overeating
items.content: The flavorful nature of the dish can lead to excess calorie intake.

items.title: Food safety
items.content: Undercooked lamb may harbor harmful bacteria; cook to an internal temperature of about 70 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the hot kabobs directly from the grill, optionally drizzling with lemon juice, fresh herbs, or a yogurt‑based sauce. They pair well with a light green salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cooked kabobs keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. Reheat thoroughly before serving. Raw meat and vegetables should be stored separately and used within 24 hours.
